abstract: The phenomenon of multiple primary malignant neoplasms involving the head and neck is well documented. Epidermoid carcinomas constitute the majority of these neoplasms. Case reports are made of two patients with simultaneously occurring chronic reticuloendothelial malignancies and non-epidermoid tumors involving the head and neck. The first case is one of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and metastatic primary retroperitoneal extragonadal seminoma, while the second is one of lymphocytic lymphoma (LL) and a carotid body tumor (CBT). The head and neck manifestations of metastatic seminoma, CBT, and CLL and LL are discussed. A review of the literature of the association of each of these entities to other tumors is presented. Also presented is the evidence for an increased incidence of malignancies associated with CLL and LL and the complicating factors introduced when reticuloendothelial malignancies occur simultaneously with head and neck neoplasms.
abstract_ja: 頭頸部における同時性の多発原発悪性腫瘍は十分に記録されており、その大部分は表皮様癌である。本報告では、慢性リンパ性白血病(CLL)と後腹膜原発性性腺外セミノーマの転移を併発した症例、およびリンパ性リンパ腫(LL)と頸動脈小体腫瘍を併発した症例の2例を報告する。転移性セミノーマ、頸動脈小体腫瘍、CLLおよびLLの頭頸部病変の所見について考察する。これらの疾患とその他の腫瘍との関連に関する文献的考察も示す。また、細網内皮系悪性腫瘍と頭頸部腫瘍が同時に生じた場合にCLLおよびLLに関連する悪性腫瘍の発生頻度が増加するという証拠と、複雑化する要因についても示す。
